d.g: To turn or open slightly; to become ajar or to cause to become ajar; to be or to hang ajar.
d.x: A plainclothes detective knocked on a slightly ajarred door.

d.g: Being at variance or in contradiction to something.
d.x: There is a sort of unexpressed concern, / A kind of shock that sets one's heart ajar […].

ajar.e: From Middle English ajar, on char (“on [the] turn”), from on (“on”) + char (“turn, occasion”), from Old English ċierr, cyrr (“turn”), from ċierran (“to turn, convert”), equivalent to a- + char. Akin to Scots char, chare (“to turn, cause to turn”), Dutch akerre, kier (“ajar”), German kehren (“to turn”). See char.

d.x: Oh, vada well that omee-palone ajax who just trolled in[.]

d.g: An ace and a jack as a starting hand in Texas hold 'em.
Any plant in the genus Ajuga, especially the ornamental ground cover Ajuga reptans.

ajuga.e: From the genus name taxonomic name Ajuga.
